title: Smallest Good Base
summary: Given an integer n as a string, find the smallest k (where k >= 2) such that n can be represented as a string of all 1s in base k.
statement: Given an integer n as a string, find the smallest k (where k >= 2) such that n can be represented as a string of all 1s in base k.
constraints: n is a decimal string with no leading zeros, representing an integer in 3..10^18.
A good integer base is at least 2 and writes n using only digit 1. Return the SMALLEST such base as a decimal string.
Two ones are allowed: base n-1 always writes n as 11. Larger numbers must not be rounded through floating-point arithmetic.
hints: For a fixed number of ones, the represented integer grows strictly with the base.
Try digit counts from longest to shortest and binary-search the base for each count using exact integers.
Evaluate 1+b+...+b^(digits-1) by total=total*b+1, stopping once total exceeds n. Fall back to n-1.
A longer valid representation uses a smaller base. Power-of-two bounds give a safe integer search interval without a floating root.
editorial: Search digit counts in descending order, then use monotonicity of the geometric sum to locate a base. There is at most one base for each count. Exact Horner evaluation avoids overflow rounding and permits early stopping. The two-digit base n-1 guarantees an answer. The small-input oracle tries every base and inspects every remainder; large cases are independently checked with exact power-root certificates.

tests.explanation: 13 = 1+3+9, so base 3 writes 111. Base 12 also writes 11, but is not the smallest.
4681 = 1+8+64+512+4096, so base 8 writes 11111; checking only two or three digits would miss it.
